findings.view: synthetic-earth.png and hover-debris-orbit.png (x 640-668, y 318-400, over the Earth disc); synthetic-8-patches.png (x 540-640, y 380-560); accept-node-added.png and accept-prograde-drag.png (the whole orbit ring around the planet)
findings.defect: Patches that lie on or within 1-2 px of each other are drawn independently, and their dashes interleave. Over the Earth in synthetic-earth.png and hover-debris-orbit.png the two planned patches running into the entry point form an 80 px zig-zag (a lightning-bolt staircase of mauve and tan dashes, each with its own dark casing). In synthetic-8-patches.png three coincident patches form a barber pole of tan and red-brown dashes with a different colour peeking out at each dash end. Right after adding a node (accept-node-added.png, Δv 0, and accept-prograde-drag.png, 10 m/s) the planned patch lies on the current orbit and the whole ring becomes a yellow / cyan / dark-teal candy stripe. This was item 14 of the previous list (minor); the dark casing added this round makes the zig-zag more visible. The fixer also reports that dashes far from the node still slide while the camera turns; no moving-camera sequence exists to check it.
findings.realReference: KSP, Juno: New Origins and Orbiter draw a planned orbit as one clean stroke; where a planned patch coincides with the current orbit only one of them is visible, and two near-coincident laps read as two parallel lines or as one, never as a jagged stair.
findings.likelyCause: src/map/scene.ts (verts.len, doc comment at lines 236 and 286-287): the dash phase is the cumulative screen length from each line's own first vertex, so two patches on the same screen path have unrelated phases. Every patch is drawn with its own casing (CASING_PX 1.25, CASING_ALPHA 0.6 in src/map/constants.ts), and nothing suppresses a patch where it is within a line width of an earlier one.
findings.fixDirection: Detect near-coincident stretches on the CPU (the line occupancy grid in src/map/lineGrid.ts already has the drawn segments): where a later patch runs within about 2 px of an earlier one for more than a dash period, draw only the higher-priority one there (planned over current, nearer in time over later), or offset the second by a full line width so the two read as parallel lines. Derive the dash phase from a parameter shared by patches on the same path (screen arc length measured from the point where they join) so the dashes coincide. Draw the casing of all lines in one pass before all cores. Record a short orbit-camera sequence of a dashed patch and check that a dash stays put.

findings.likelyCause: src/map/controller.ts lines 1555-1557 build the icon list as plates, then icons, then gizmo, so every icon is drawn after every plate. Add a browser check in the synthetic Earth view that no debris-coloured pixel lies inside a label rectangle from describe().

findings.view: real-lowOrbit.png (orbit ends in black at (818,246)); real-lowOrbit-node.png (gizmo at (790,224) and dashed orbit ending at (428,370), both against black); real-lunarOrbit.png (orbit ends at (832,315), Moon-orbit line ends at (768,210), Tranquility Base pin at (832,351) on black)
findings.defect: Over the real renderer the night hemisphere is pure black, the same value as space (sampled (0,0,0) at ten points inside the Earth's night disc; 1-8 of 255 on the Moon). The map cuts lines at a limb the viewer cannot see, so the vessel's orbit stops in mid-air, the planet looks bitten, and the gizmo of a node behind the planet floats in the void with its 'behind the body' ring referring to nothing visible. In three of the five real-planet pictures a trajectory ends in empty space.
findings.realReference: out/qa/ref/earth-orbit-clouds/airglow-red-yellow.jpg and limb-panorama.jpg: the real night limb is outlined by a thin airglow shell (peak Y 0.16 against sky Y 0.008), so the planet's edge is never invisible. Shipped maps go further: KSP lights bodies with a map-mode ambient and Orbiter draws a disc outline, so the silhouette that hides a line is always on screen.
findings.likelyCause: The overlay draws nothing for a body larger than the icon threshold (SMALL_OBJECT_PX 6 in src/map/constants.ts) and relies on the backdrop to show the disc. The lab sphere has an ambient term, so the lab pictures hide the problem; the real planet at flight exposure has none on the night side.
findings.fixDirection: In drawOverlay draw a thin silhouette ring for every body whose disc is on screen (1 px, body colour at 25-35 % alpha, radius from the same analytic disc the occlusion test uses), or a faint night-side fill. Alternatively file a request for a map-mode ambient in the planet renderer. Consider keeping the hidden part of the active trajectory as a faint dotted stroke instead of nothing. Add real-lowOrbit night-side and real-lunarOrbit assertions that pixels on the predicted limb differ from the background.

findings.view: real-lowOrbit-dayside.png (pad icon at (269,227), label x 285-550, y 219-236)
findings.defect: The launch-site label 'Ka Lae Pacific Spaceport, Launch Complex 1' is a ghost: plate and text are drawn at roughly 40 % alpha over white cloud. Measured: brightest text pixel (149,151,155) on a plate median of (86,92,104), about 2.3:1, with the cloud behind at (107,113,130). The green zone ring shows through the plate between 'Lae' and 'Pacific'. The pad is 3-5 px inside the limb, and at 1x time it stays there for minutes, so this is a lasting state, not a transition.
findings.realReference: Shipped maps show a label fully or not at all: text on a bright planet keeps 4.5:1 or better on its plate until the marker is hidden, then goes in a short timed fade.
findings.likelyCause: src/map/controller.ts line 1431: a = (1 - t.hidden) * ..., passed as the label alpha at line 1438; line 1536 draws the plate with COLORS.plate (alpha 0.7, constants.ts line 176) times that alpha, so a marker half-way through the 1.5 px limb fade gets a 28 % plate and 40 % text.
findings.fixDirection: Do not scale label or plate alpha by partial occlusion: keep both at full strength while the anchor is visible at all, then hide the label (a timed fade over 150-200 ms). Let only the icon follow the spatial fade. Apply the same rule to marker, vessel and body labels (lines 1240, 1264, 1290, 1314).

findings.view: accept-panel.png (Ap markers at (535,431) and (555,458); labels 'Ap 200.0 km / T-44m 10s' at x 447-520, y 443-472 and 'Ap 371.5 km / T-2h 17m 03s' at x 570-655, y 418-446)
findings.defect: Two apoapsis markers sit 33 px apart and their labels read crosswise. The marker at (555,458) is opposite the node, so it is the planned apoapsis (371.5 km), but the label level with it and 35 px to its left says 'Ap 200.0 km'. The marker at (535,431) is the current orbit's apoapsis (200 km), and the label level with it to the right says 'Ap 371.5 km'. Each label is in fact attached to its own marker by a corner (11 px diagonal offset), with no leader, so a reader pairs them by row and gets the wrong value. The 371.5 km label also sits over the planet disc instead of outside the orbit.
findings.realReference: KSP prints the apsis value against its own marker and shows the planned apsis in the planned-orbit colour; where two markers are close, shipped maps attach each label with a leader or tint so the pairing is never ambiguous.
findings.likelyCause: src/map/labels.ts lines 242-298: the diagonal candidates (cases 4-7) put a plate corner at e = 0.75 * (clear + gap) from the anchor; a candidate is rejected only if it overlaps an icon, never because it is level with or nearer to a different icon. src/map/controller.ts line 1537 draws a leader only for the outer ring (b.far). Both labels use the same text colour.
findings.fixDirection: Draw a short leader or corner tick for every placement that is not directly beside its anchor. In declutter, add a cost when the candidate's nearest icon is not its own anchor, and prefer the outer side of the anchor's own line. Tint the first label line with the patch colour (current cyan, planned yellow) so the two apsides differ at a glance.

findings.view: synthetic-moon-intercept.png ('Enter Moon' label x 938-1025, y 375-405); accept-panel.png ('Node 1' plate over the orbit at x 558-600, y 245-262); synthetic-moon.png and hover-impact-details.png ('Impact ...' plate over the dashed exit patch at x 560-600, y 325-345); accept-translunar.png ('Moon' plate over the Moon's orbit line at x 704-735, y 598)
findings.defect: Labels still land on lines, including their own. The solid trajectory that ends at the 'Enter Moon' marker runs through the first text row of that label: (62,52,38) under the plate against (190,148,88) outside it, about 30 % visible. The Node 1 plate hides about 25 px of the orbit next to the node being edited. The plate masks rather than avoids, and at 70 % it does not fully mask.
findings.realReference: Shipped maps place a marker label on the outer side of its own trajectory; a plate is the fallback, and it is opaque.
findings.likelyCause: The fixer dropped line avoidance for cost (hand-off: labels avoid only their own line by side preference). The preference is a sort order over the eight candidates (labels.ts lines 221-238), not a test against the polyline, so a candidate along the line is taken when the others are blocked. COLORS.plate alpha is 0.7.
findings.fixDirection: Test each candidate rectangle against the anchor's own patch polyline (a few segments near the anchor, not the whole grid) and against the active trajectory; cache the result while the scene is unchanged. Raise the plate to at least 0.9 alpha.

In the top view the limb-side arc of the Central Pacific ring is a pale half-faded ghost beside the full-strength inner arc.

findings.likelyCause: The casing of one segment is drawn over the core of its neighbour at the ring's seam (src/map/scene.ts addZoneLine / the seam join); the arc lying exactly on the horizon sits inside the 1.5 px occlusion fade for its whole length.
